correctness.rationale: In the scalar source specialization, the auxiliary problem is exactly \(axY+\tfrac12Y^2\), so \(Y=-ax\). Direct substitution into the published Wolfe inequalities gives the necessary and sufficient interval \(1-\gamma\le\alpha a\le2(1-\beta)\). The source grid has \(\alpha\le1\), which proves necessity of \(a\ge1-\gamma\); sufficiency follows from the factor-two spacing and the strict inequality \(1-\beta>1-\gamma\). The explicit example has a nonempty continuous Wolfe interval \([2,12]\) and no source-grid point.

value.rationale: The obstruction occurs on the simplest strongly convex quadratic and is caused purely by scale, not by nonsmooth uncertainty or multiobjective geometry. It separates the source's valid continuous Wolfe-existence theorem from the actual discrete algorithm and gives an exact if-and-only-if definedness frontier. The two-sided dyadic repair is minimal, preserves geometric trial scaling, and explains why standard Wolfe searches include an expansion/bracketing phase.
